allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge: about a metre by 60 years, 1.5 to 2 m by 110. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: 18 to 30 ribs, areoles close together, red to yellow-tipped radials and four long, curved but never hooked centrals that cover the body, greying with age. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): its tepals on a spiral (their count by hand: no flora counts them) on a floral cup above the inferior ovary, and a style with 13 to 20 stigma lobes, from the characters of Cactaceae and Ferocactus by the rules at the flowering plants. Its 200 stamens by hand, the most a flower draws, for the numerous ones every flora gives.

appearance.bodies.stem.spines.central.le.note: Spec rework E6c: the cacti's ribs, areoles and spines grown from the characters their floras state, in each body look that has ribs or a spine set of that role.

appearance.organs.flower.shape.carpels.note: How PlantGen draws a flower, a choice of the model's (spec rework P5): the flower characters set a flower card's perianth, its parts, how they differ by place, how far the corolla is joined into a tube, a floral cup, where the ovary sits, a resupinate flower's turn, its stamens, staminodes and carpels and its spurs. The rules also set these fields in a season's flower and bud looks that draw a flower, unless set there by hand.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a single cylindrical barrel up to 2 to 2.5 m tall and 25 to 40 cm across, leaning a little south, so densely spined that the green body hardly shows. Yellow flowers in a crown ring in spring and dry yellow fruit. Not fitted to measurements.

generator.params.dioecious.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant bears both sexes, unless its taxa state it dioecious.

generator.params.height_max.note: What the conifer and succulent programs' height_max means: the height their Chapman-Richards curve rises toward with age and never reaches, so the tallest the plant grows, the height a flora gives as its greatest ("trees to 40 m"). Plants of a usual age stand below it, as the curve says. Where a flora's greatest is a rare record, the plant grows a little tall; a check of the grown plant against its usual height (spec rework M8) will show it.

generator.params.sex.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant's sex is its own draw, dealt across a package's seeds so that both sexes grow; the typical plant (sex 0.5) is female, so it shows its fruit.

generator.program.note: The cacti's own program (growth plan G2.3a): columns, barrels and chains of joints, their ribs, areoles and spines from each species' look.

generator.spreads.params.height_max.note: What the conifer and succulent programs' height_max means: the height their Chapman-Richards curve rises toward with age and never reaches, so the tallest the plant grows, the height a flora gives as its greatest ("trees to 40 m"). growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

taxon.note: Common name (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.genus.note: The genus WCVP v16's accepted name is written in.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted subspecies the name resolves to (the accepted name).

taxon.scientific_name.note: WCVP v16's accepted name for the plant the spec's authors wrote as Ferocactus cylindraceus, which WCVP treats as a synonym.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy (milestone F1). Calibration against measurements and photographs comes later.
